post.caption: Plaster cracked, and solid gold showed. This is the Golden Buddha of Wat Traimit in Bangkok. Its style comes from the Sukhothai period of Thai art, and nobody knows exactly when it was made. Scholars suspect plaster was added to keep it safe. In 1955, workers lifted it to move it to a new hall. The statue was dropped, and some plaster chipped off. Underneath, the statue was solid gold. The rest of the plaster was then removed. The statue holds about 5.5 metric tons of gold and is about 3 meters tall. It is kept in a marble hall in Bangkok's Chinatown.
